answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity flow through accountable introductions: a newcomer enters only through an inlet, an existing member who publicly signs for it with a quill of cryptographic endorsement and puts its own reputation on the line. If the newcomer cheats, the sponsor loses standing too, so invitations stay scarce and careful. Over time trust grows like a vine along these verified links, and isolated clusters with no reputable sponsor simply cannot reach the shared market.
